transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-22 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Recording: (Fireflies auto)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Lopez (Redwood CSM); Daniel Ruiz (Constellation Head of Cloud), Priya Nambiar (Solutions Architect), Liam O'Connor (Marketplace PM), Aisha Khan (Security)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick round of intros? I'll hand it over to Daniel to give a little context on Constellation's marketplace strategy.
[00:12] Daniel Ruiz: Yeah, thanks Maya. Um, short context - we run a vendor marketplace inside Constellation that we launched last year. Goal is to surface partner services that provision into our customer VPCs and do billing via our platform. We're exploring Redwood for a managed inference offering that we can list so our customers can spin up Redwood-managed LLM endpoints within Constellation accounts.
[00:36] Maya Chen: Awesome. From Redwood side, Omar and I will cover integration points - listing content, reference architecture for private deployments (VPC peering vs PrivateLink), and what we need for security review. Sofia will own the pilot/co-sell ops.
[00:51] Omar Patel: Hi all, quick note - we'll also include notes about quantization/latency profiles and dedicated capacity options because some enterprise buyers ask about per-token latency and burst behavior.
[01:05] Liam O'Connor: Quick Q - what's the expected deployment model when a Constellation customer clicks "deploy"? Do they get a Redwood tenant in our cloud, or do we provision into their own AWS account?
[01:18] Omar Patel: Great question. There are two patterns we typically support: hosted (Redwood-managed in our multi-tenant infra) and private deployment where a Redwood control plane can orchestrate workloads into a customer's VPC or a dedicated account. For marketplace we'll probably want a private VPC-based reference arch so deployments can land in the customer's cloud with appropriate data controls.
[01:40] Priya Nambiar: When you say "control plane orchestrate," do you mean a customer-managed control plane or Redwood retains the control plane? We have procurement + security preferences around who holds keys and network access.
[01:51] Omar Patel: We support both flavors. For the Constellation listing the common pattern is Redwood control plane in a customer-specific account but with customer-managed keys (KMS) and audit logs forwarded to the customer's Splunk/CloudWatch. We can also offer fully air-gapped on-prem in extreme cases.
[02:08] Aisha Khan: Can you confirm what encryption at rest looks like? We require CMK by default for marketplace offerings. SOC2 alignment is a hard ask for us.
[02:18] Maya Chen: Yep - we can use customer KMS (bring-your-own-key) for data at rest. We'll attach our SOC2 Type II report and provide the security questionnaire. Omar, you flagged any technical caveats?
[02:27] Omar Patel: Two things to flag: 1) KV cache and prefix caching behaviour - if caching is enabled in a shared routing layer we surface metadata, so we recommend cache to be isolated per-customer. 2) When provisioning into customer VPC we need either PrivateLink endpoints or VPC peering; PrivateLink tends to be simpler for cross-account access but has egress considerations.
[02:45] Daniel Ruiz: We prefer PrivateLink usually, less routing churn for our infra team.
[02:49] Maya Chen: Noted. Liam, for marketplace listing content, typical inputs we need are: logo, description, quickstart steps, pricing SKU, supported regions, and any infra prerequisites (like required IAM roles or subnets).
[03:03] Liam O'Connor: Ok, we do have a listing template - I'll share it. Important note: our billing flow wants a per-hour subscription SKU with usage-based overage. Do you support metered billing integration?
[03:15] Maya Chen: We can integrate in three ways: 1) Redwood invoices Constellation directly and Constellation bills customers, 2) Redwood supports metered billing via marketplace APIs (we've integrated with a couple of vendors), or 3) hybrid where the first month is subscription and token overage billed separately. We'll document options in the listing draft.
[03:34] Priya Nambiar: On the infra side, we use Terraform modules to standardize provisioning. Can you provide TF modules or Helm charts?
[03:42] Omar Patel: Yes, we have reference Terraform modules and Helm charts for operator-based installs. We'll include a sample module that provisions the control plane role, endpoints and minimal security groups. The customer will need to supply role ARN and KMS key ARN.
[03:55] [00:04:00] (Speaker overlap / unclear)
[03:58] Aisha Khan: For compliance, we'll need access to audit logs and to show that no PII is persisted outside the customer's region. Is region pinning possible?
[04:08] Omar Patel: Region pinning is supported - you can pin workloads to specified regions and we can publish region matrix per model. Quantized model variants might only be available in specific regions, we'll include that caveat.
[04:19] Daniel Ruiz: On the sales ops side, what files do you need from us to draft the listing?
[04:24] Maya Chen: If Liam can share the listing template, and Priya can share TF modules + egress/security constraints, we'll draft the marketplace content and the reference architecture diagram. We'll also attach security artifacts: SOC2, penetration test summary, and our KMS integration notes.
[04:36] Liam O'Connor: I'll loop in legal to confirm contract language for marketplace revenue share. That might impact pricing SKU.
[04:43] Sofia Lopez: From CSM ops, we'll coordinate pilot customers and an onboarding plan. Suggested pilot window is 4-6 weeks with two internal workloads to validate latency and costs.
[04:56] Priya Nambiar: For the deployment workshop, we want to walk through permission boundaries and the Terraform flow end-to-end. Also, how rollbacks are handled in your control plane if a model push fails.
[05:08] Omar Patel: Rollbacks are handled at the model versioning layer; we support canary traffic splits and automatic fallback to previous model variants if there's a runtime regression. We'll include playbook steps in the deployment doc.
[05:20] [00:05:20] Priya Nambiar: A practical question - what are the typical time-to-provision numbers? From our side, we need to set expectations for customers.
[05:26] Omar Patel: For a private deployment onto a customer's VPC, assuming IAM and endpoints are provisioned, we've seen 20-40 minutes to stand up a control plane and initial endpoints. Model download/quantization can be extra depending on model size; we recommend pre-warming popular model bundles for marketplace entries.
[05:42] Aisha Khan: Do you have HSM integrations for key signing? Some of our regulated customers insist on HSM-backed signing.
[05:48] Maya Chen: We integrate with cloud KMS providers; for HSM-specific workflows we can discuss an on-prem or dedicated customer deployment. We'll put HSM as a supported option in the security section.
[06:00] Daniel Ruiz: Any blockers on the Redwood side for listing?
[06:04] Maya Chen: None major. We need the Constellation listing template and confirmation on billing path. Also will need answers to the security questionnaire.
[06:12] Liam O'Connor: I'll send the template by EOD and add the legal contact.
[06:17] Maya Chen: Great. One more technical note - when customers spin up the offering via the marketplace, do you expect a single-click UX that provisions infra automatically or a guided workflow with manual approvals?
[06:29] Liam O'Connor: Preference is single-click but with an option for approval gates for enterprise accounts. We can build in an IAM role assumption flow.
[06:36] Omar Patel: We can support both. For single-click we use a CloudFormation/Terraform automation path. For approval gates we toggle a flag in Constellation's provisioning service.
[06:47] [00:07:00] (crosstalk)
[06:50] Priya Nambiar: A note on network: we will want to inspect egress patterns; PrivateLink endpoints would keep egress within Constellation but there are NAT & route table details to verify.
[07:00] Omar Patel: We'll provide sample security groups and route table guidance in the ref-arch.
[07:05] Maya Chen: Okay quick recap and explicit next steps then we'll wrap.
[07:09] Maya Chen: Actions: Redwood to draft listing + ref arch and send by 2025-07-25; Omar to create deployment playbook + TF/Helm examples by 2025-07-29; Constellation to return security answers and share marketplace template by 2025-07-28; schedule workshop for week of Aug 4th.
[07:27] Daniel Ruiz: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[07:30] Liam O'Connor: I'll follow up with the legal thread and the template.
[07:32] Aisha Khan: I'll prepare the SOC2 scoping and send a short list of mandatory controls.
[07:36] Maya Chen: Great — we'll send the draft listing and a short checklist. Thanks all.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings noted (e.g., "KV cash" in one segment should read "KV cache"), speaker labels sometimes generic from auto-transcript.
